description: Machine-readable live work queue. Passing entries are retained for 24 hours, then removed by pnpm features:prune; durable behavior and evidence remain in product specs and Git/PR history. See docs/FEATURES.md for rules.

features.behavior: `npx <connection-url>` (e.g. `npx mongodb://localhost:27017/qyre_test` or `npx postgres://...`) fails with npm's own EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL error because npx parses the argument as a package spec before qyre ever runs. The CLI gains an interactive guided-login flow for users who hit this or simply run `npx qyre` with no target: pick an engine, then enter user, a masked password (echoed as ****), host, port, and database; on a failed connection attempt, show the real error and offer retry (Y) or quit (N) rather than exiting. Startup help/output also explains the npx protocol:// pitfall directly and points at the correct `npx qyre <connection-url>` shape or this new interactive prompt.
features.verification: pnpm --filter qyre test
features.evidence: PR #90 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/90), pushed as c283172. Added a `--login` flag that skips the connection-string argument and prompts interactively for engine (Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB), user, masked password, host, port, and database, retrying the connect attempt (Y/N) on failure. A target given directly with no username (e.g. `postgres://host:5432/db`) is now prompted for just the missing credentials, but only when stdin is a TTY, so piped/non-interactive invocations are unaffected. `--help` explains the npx protocol:// pitfall and points at `--login`; the no-target startup banner hints at it too. `connectToRaw` now also calls `adapter.ping()` after `connect()` (mirroring `/api/connect`'s own check from F085), since Postgres/MySQL's `connect()` only builds a lazy pool and would otherwise resolve against an unreachable host, defeating the retry prompt. New `packages/cli/src/guided-login.ts` (pure, injectable `GuidedLoginPrompts`) and `guided-login-io.ts` (real stdin/stdout wiring with raw-mode password masking and a persistent leftover buffer so a single chunk containing multiple piped answers isn't dropped past the first newline). Verified with `pnpm --filter qyre test` (44 passed) and `pnpm verify:pr` (checks, build, smoke + full E2E across PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQLite/MongoDB). GitHub CI passed both End-to-end and Lint/typecheck/test/build.

features.behavior: Local-server authentication and browser hardening, landing FIRST in plan 0006 because it protects even the read-only product and is a precondition for any mutating route: the CLI mints a cryptographically random per-session token at startup, the served UI receives it (injected into index.html or fetched via a one-time bootstrap), and every /api route rejects requests without it (401, structured error) - closing the current no-auth surface where any local process/user can call the full API and where cross-origin CSRF is blocked only implicitly by Fastify's JSON content-type requirement (pgweb/DbGate precedent for local web DB tools). Security headers land with it: CSP on the served SPA (also neutralizes DB-data-driven request exfil via F086's image URL previews), X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options. Open decision (exec plan 0006 #3): header-based token + fetch/blob downloads vs cookie - the CSV export links (plain <a href>) must keep working, so the choice must cover download URLs. E2E: UI works end-to-end with the token; a tokenless curl to every /api route 401s; docs/SECURITY.md updated. No dependency on other plan slices.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @qyre/server test && pnpm --filter qyre test && pnpm test:e2e
features.evidence: PR #94 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/94), pushed as 339010d. Added @qyre/server/src/services/auth-token.ts (crypto.randomBytes token, constant-time compare) and two new plugins: auth-guard.ts (rejects any /api/* request without a valid token - Authorization: Bearer header, or a ?token= query param for the CSV export's plain <a href> download, which can't set headers) and security-headers.ts (CSP with connect-src/script-src/default-src locked to 'self' but img-src open to http/https for the F086 previews, plus X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and X-Frame-Options: DENY). createServer generates a random token per instance (or accepts one via options for tests) and decorates it onto the FastifyInstance; static-web.ts now serves index.html dynamically (explicit / and /index.html routes plus the SPA-fallback notFoundHandler) with the token injected as window.__QYRE_TOKEN__, replacing @fastify/static's raw index-file serving. apps/web's fetchJson attaches the token as an Authorization header (read via a new shared/api/auth-token.ts); exportRowsUrl appends it as a query param for the real-navigation CSV download. Resolved a cross-package typecheck gap along the way: a standalone types/fastify.d.ts augmentation file wasn't visible when @qyre/qyre's own tsc run pulled in server/src/app.ts transitively (each package's tsconfig only includes its own src) - moved the `declare module "fastify"` block inline into app.ts, which is always part of every consumer's compiled unit. Updated all ~59 existing app.inject call sites across 8 test files to send an auth header via a new tests/helpers/auth.ts; added auth-guard.test.ts, security-headers.test.ts, token-injection cases in static-web.test.ts, and e2e/auth-token.spec.ts (tokenless/invalid-token 401s, real browser UI still works end-to-end - all 4 engine projects). docs/SECURITY.md updated. Verified: pnpm --filter @qyre/server test (83 passed), pnpm --filter qyre test / pnpm --filter @qyre/qyre test (44 passed), pnpm test:e2e, pnpm check:quiet, pnpm verify:pr (full local gate incl. @full E2E against live Postgres/MySQL/SQLite/MongoDB). GitHub CI passed both End-to-end and Lint/typecheck/test/build.

features.behavior: Product-spec pass for the role-aware permission/capability model before any implementation: create docs/product-specs/permissions-and-capabilities.md covering the two-tier model (session-level ConnectionCapabilities extending F063's AdapterCapabilities with supportsRowMutations/supportsDdl/supportsIndexManagement/supportsDatabaseManagement/supportsTransactions plus a readOnlyReason of qyre-flag|replica|connection|grants|null, and per-table select/insert/update/delete TablePermissions attached to TableMetadata), the per-engine introspection matrix (Postgres has_table_privilege/pg_is_in_recovery/default_transaction_read_only, MySQL information_schema privileges + role grants + @@global.read_only, SQLite file+directory writability/PRAGMA query_only/mode=ro, MongoDB connectionStatus showPrivileges action sets), the advisory-introspection/authoritative-database principle with degradation to read-only on introspection failure, the API-shape decision (extend GET /api/overview vs a new endpoint - leaning extended overview), and how the UI adapts per access level. Follow the spec pattern of F063-F066. Architectural decisions are pre-settled in docs/exec-plans/active/0006-role-aware-database-ide.md; this spec turns them into a reviewable product contract with acceptance criteria.

features.evidence: PR #95 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/95), pushed as 32affa0. Added docs/product-specs/permissions-and-capabilities.md: the two-tier ConnectionCapabilities (session-level, extends F063's AdapterCapabilities with supportsRowMutations/supportsDdl/supportsIndexManagement/supportsDatabaseManagement/supportsTransactions/readOnlyReason) / TablePermissions (per-table select/insert/update/delete, optional on TableMetadata) data contract, the per-engine introspection matrix (which native mechanism each of Postgres/MySQL/SQLite/MongoDB reads for each tier, plus each engine's restricted test fixture), and the advisory-introspection/authoritative-database principle (database always the real enforcer; introspection failure degrades to read-only never assumed-writable; --read-only always wins). features.evidence: PR #96 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/96), pushed as 050e92c. @qyre/core gains ConnectionCapabilities (extends F063's AdapterCapabilities) and TablePermissions per docs/product-specs/permissions-and-capabilities.md; DatabaseOverview.capabilities is now ConnectionCapabilities and TableMetadata gains optional permissions?: TablePermissions. DatabaseAdapter (packages/drivers/contract) gains a required getCapabilities(): Promise<ConnectionCapabilities>; a new shared stubReadOnlyCapabilities(supportsSql) helper gives every adapter (Postgres/MySQL/SQLite/MongoDB) an interim implementation - every write flag hardcoded false, readOnlyReason 'grants' - until each engine's own introspection slice (F092-F095) lands; each adapter's getOverview() now calls its own getCapabilities() instead of inlining a literal. features.behavior: Batched schema introspection, landing BEFORE per-engine permission work multiplies the current fan-out: GET /api/tables today calls getTable per table - each >= 4 catalog queries plus a row-count estimate (with a possible exact COUNT(*) fallback) - through an unbounded Promise.all (packages/server/src/routes/tables.ts), which hammers large databases and was already tracked as tech debt. Adapters gain a batched all-tables metadata path (e.g. getAllTables(): one/few set-based catalog queries per engine - information_schema joins on Postgres/MySQL, sqlite_master + per-table pragmas with bounded concurrency on SQLite, listCollections + capped sampling on MongoDB); the route uses it; getTable stays for single-table use. Row-count estimates become part of the batched query (pg_class.reltuples, information_schema.TABLES.TABLE_ROWS) rather than per-table round trips. Conformance asserts the batched path returns the same shape as N x getTable on every engine. F092-F095 attach per-table permissions to this batched path. Depends on F091.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @qyre/server test && node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test
features.evidence: PR #98 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/98), pushed as 183cb3a. DatabaseAdapter gains getAllTables(): TableMetadata[] in the same shape N getTable() calls would produce. Postgres/MySQL each get one batched query for columns, PK/FK, and indexes across every table (information_schema, no per-table filter); row counts batch too - Postgres keeps getTable()'s reltuples-estimate-with-exact-fallback semantics exactly (one estimate query, then a targeted exact COUNT(*) only for never-ANALYZEd tables), MySQL uses a single UNION ALL of exact COUNT(*) per table rather than the originally-suggested information_schema.TABLES.TABLE_ROWS estimate, since that can lag right after insert and would break exact parity with getTable() (a documented engineering deviation from the feature's literal text, made for correctness/determinism). SQLite/MongoDB have no cross-table catalog query for either engine (pragmas and field-sampling are inherently per-table/collection) - the batching win there is moving the fan-out from the route's unbounded Promise.all into a bounded sequential loop inside the adapter that reuses getTable(), correct by construction. GET /api/tables (packages/server/src/routes/tables.ts) now calls getAllTables() directly instead of getOverview() + Promise.all(getTable). A @qyre/testing-conformance case asserts the batched path returns the exact same shape as calling getTable() per table, live against all 4 engines. Verified: pnpm --filter @qyre/server test (84 passed), pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test (48 passed, incl. the new parity test), each adapter's own test suite unchanged, pnpm check:quiet, pnpm verify:pr (full local gate incl. @full E2E against live Postgres/MySQL/SQLite/MongoDB - Schema tab exercises getAllTables() end-to-end). GitHub CI passed both End-to-end and Lint/typecheck/test/build.

features.behavior: Tables and views become distinct kinds - a modeling gap the write stage would trip over: all three SQL drivers read information_schema.tables (or sqlite_master) with no table_type filter today, so views appear as ordinary editable 'tables'. TableMetadata (and the batched F123 path) gains kind: 'table' | 'view' | 'materialized-view' | 'collection' (Postgres pg_class.relkind/table_type incl. matviews - which information_schema misses - MySQL TABLE_TYPE, SQLite sqlite_master.type, MongoDB collection vs view from listCollections). The UI shows a subtle kind badge in the sidebar/schema views; every later mutation/DDL surface gates on kind (editing a view's rows, DROP TABLE on a view, truncating a matview are all prevented up front with the reason stated). Read-only behavior otherwise unchanged. Conformance: a fixture view per SQL engine (and a MongoDB view) reports its kind correctly everywhere. Depends on F123.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @qyre/server test && node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test && pnpm --filter @qyre/ui test
features.evidence: PR #99 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/99), pushed as 2ac72f1. TableMetadata gains a required kind: 'table' | 'view' | 'materialized-view' | 'collection'. Fixed two real visibility gaps beyond mistagging: Postgres materialized views were entirely invisible before (information_schema.tables has no concept of them - now sourced from pg_class directly, relkind IN ('r','p','f','v','m')); SQLite views were entirely excluded from every listing (WHERE type = 'table' only - now type IN ('table','view')). Postgres/MySQL derive kind from the same batched listing query F123 already built (pg_class.relkind / information_schema.tables.table_type), no extra round trip; SQLite from sqlite_master.type; MongoDB from listCollections' previously-discarded type field. Row counts skip views entirely across all four engines (a view's reltuples/TABLE_ROWS is meaningless with no storage of its own, and COUNT(*) would silently re-execute the underlying query). The Schema tab's TableDetail card (already receives full TableMetadata, zero plumbing) shows a subtle VIEW/MATERIALIZED VIEW badge, omitted for the unremarkable default (table/collection) per engine. Deliberately deferred: the sidebar tree badge - SchemaMetadata.tables is bare string[] today, and threading kind through it would mean changing that type across all four adapters' getOverview() output plus every existing test asserting on that shape, a materially larger change than this slice needs; the Schema tab (the primary place kind matters for future DDL/mutation gating) is covered. A @qyre/testing-conformance case creates a real view (and a MongoDB view via viewOn) per engine and asserts kind is correct via both getTable() and the batched getAllTables() path, live against all 4 engines. Verified: pnpm --filter @qyre/server test (84 passed), pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test (52 passed, incl. new view-fixture kind assertions), pnpm --filter @qyre/ui test (159 passed, incl. 4 new TableDetail badge render tests), each adapter's own test suite unchanged, pnpm check:quiet, pnpm verify:pr (full local gate incl. @full E2E against live Postgres/MySQL/SQLite/MongoDB). GitHub CI passed both End-to-end and Lint/typecheck/test/build. Live browser screenshot of the badge wasn't possible in this environment (Claude in Chrome extension unreachable) - verified via the 4 component-level render tests instead.

features.behavior: Postgres permission introspection per the F090 spec: getCapabilities() reports real session writability (pg_is_in_recovery(), default_transaction_read_only, role attributes from pg_roles, has_database_privilege/has_schema_privilege CREATE checks), and getTable plus the batched F123 all-tables path attach per-table TablePermissions via has_table_privilege(current_user, ..., 'SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE') batched per schema (one set-based query, not per-table round trips; works uniformly for tables and views). Introspection failure degrades to read-only with a logged warning, never to assumed-writable. Adds a restricted qyre_readonly Postgres user (SELECT-only grants) to the docker-compose init and @qyre/testing so integration tests cover both access levels from now on. Depends on F091, F123.

features.behavior: MySQL permission introspection per the F090 spec: getCapabilities() reports session writability (@@global.read_only, @@session.transaction_read_only) and getTable/the batched F123 path attach per-table TablePermissions by unioning information_schema.USER_PRIVILEGES, SCHEMA_PRIVILEGES, and TABLE_PRIVILEGES - PLUS role-granted privileges, which those three tables omit entirely: use ROLE_TABLE_GRANTS/ROLE_SCHEMA_GRANTS (MySQL 8.0.19+) for currently-active roles, falling back to grants-only introspection (degrade toward read-only, log a warning) on older servers where role visibility is unavailable. A grant at any broader level implies the table-level right; the union must be tested explicitly since MySQL scatters grants across all these levels. Adds a restricted qyre_readonly MySQL user (SELECT-only) plus a role-granted-writer fixture user to the docker-compose init and @qyre/testing. Depends on F091, F123.
features.verification: node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/mysql test && node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test

features.behavior: SQLite writability introspection per the F090 spec: getCapabilities() reflects whether the session can write at all - the database file AND its directory must be writable (WAL/journal files need directory write), PRAGMA query_only must be off, and a ?mode=ro/immutable open flag forces read-only; per-table TablePermissions are uniform (SQLite has no users/grants - the whole file is writable or not) and must say so via the capabilities shape rather than faking per-table variance. Tests cover a writable file, a chmod-read-only file, a read-only directory, and a mode=ro target. Depends on F091, F123.

features.behavior: MongoDB permission introspection per the F090 spec: getCapabilities() and per-collection TablePermissions derive from connectionStatus{showPrivileges:true} - mapping find/insert/update/remove and createCollection/dropCollection/createIndex/dropIndex actions per db/collection resource (including anyResource and db-level wildcards); an unauthenticated local connection (no authenticatedUsers) is full-access, matching mongod's real behavior; introspection failure degrades to read-only with a logged warning. Adds a restricted fixture user with the built-in read role on the test db to the mongo init and @qyre/testing. Depends on F091, F123.

features.behavior: Product-spec pass for row-level editing before implementation: create docs/product-specs/row-editing.md covering the structured mutation API (typed JSON translated to parameterized SQL or MongoDB collection ops inside each adapter - the F072 filter pattern; the browser never builds SQL), row identity rules (full primary key required, composite keys supported, MongoDB uses _id; PK-less tables and any kind !== 'table'/'collection' (F124 views/matviews) stay read-only with the reason surfaced), and the two editing surfaces settled in exec plan 0006: SQL engines use grid editing with a pending-changes buffer + generated-statement preview + transactional batch commit; MongoDB uses whole-document Extended JSON editing (Compass model) because flat cell edits cannot express nested documents and display values are already serialized (dates as ISO strings per F081, ObjectId as hex) - the spec must fix the EJSON flavor (relaxed vs canonical) and changed-fields-update vs document-replace semantics (exec plan 0006 open decision #1, the highest-risk decision in the plan). Also: value validation/coercion per column type reusing F082/F089 capability classification, the commit endpoint shape (open decision #5), the audit-event contract, and confirmation thresholds per docs/SECURITY.md. Depends on F090, F124.

features.behavior: Structured row insert across all four engines per docs/product-specs/row-editing.md: the adapter mutations namespace gains insertRow - SQL engines take a flat column->value map translated to a parameterized INSERT; MongoDB takes an Extended JSON document parsed server-side to real BSON (per the F098 spec's EJSON decision) passed to insertOne - with value coercion per column type and the inserted row/key reported where the engine supports it. The server adds POST /api/tables/:schema/:table/rows, validating the body with Zod against the table's real introspected columns (same injection-surface pattern as F065/F072), rejecting kind !== 'table'/'collection' targets (F124), gated by both the F096 central guard and the table's insert permission, and logging a structured audit event (EventLog + pino, per exec plan decision 8). Conformance cases cover successful insert plus rejections (read-only session, unknown column, view target, restricted fixture user) on all four engines. Depends on F096, F098.

features.behavior: Structured row update per docs/product-specs/row-editing.md: the mutations namespace gains updateRowByKey requiring a full primary-key match (composite keys supported; MongoDB matches _id), rejecting tables without a primary key and kind !== 'table'/'collection' targets, parameterized everywhere; SQL engines take a flat changes map; MongoDB takes the F098-specced document-update payload (changed-fields or replace, per the spec decision) parsed from EJSON server-side. Zero-rows-matched is reported as a distinct outcome (stale row), never as silent success. Server route (PATCH on the rows resource) gated by guard + update permission, audited, with the same column-validation pattern as F099. features.behavior: Batch commit for the SQL pending-changes model per docs/product-specs/row-editing.md: one endpoint applies an ordered set of staged inserts/updates/deletes wrapped in a single transaction on Postgres/MySQL/SQLite (all-or-nothing; rollback on first failure with the failing op index reported). MongoDB is deliberately NOT part of this endpoint - its document editor (F125) saves per-document, per the exec plan's decision 5. Adapters gain the transactional wrapper in their mutations namespace; the server validates every op against introspected columns/permissions/kind before starting, and audits the batch outcome. Conformance: mixed-batch success and mid-batch failure rollback on the three SQL engines; MongoDB asserts the endpoint cleanly reports not-applicable. Depends on F101.
